body.v1n1-04-peatland-carbon.intro.0: Peatlands are the only type of terrestrial ecosystem capable of accumulating carbon in the form of peat over millennia. At the same time, they are a natural source of methane, a greenhouse gas with a high global warming potential. The net climatic effect of a peatland is determined by the balance between these processes and is sensitive to the water table level.
body.v1n1-04-peatland-carbon.intro.1: Drainage of peatlands for peat extraction, agriculture and forestry turns them from a sink into a source of CO₂. The growing interest in the restoration (rewetting) of disturbed peatlands as a climate measure calls for reliable methods of assessing the carbon balance. The aim of this review is to compare existing methods, their capabilities and limitations.
body.v1n1-04-peatland-carbon.methods.0: Publications were searched for in bibliographic databases using combinations of the keywords “peat bog”, “carbon balance”, “CO₂ flux”, “methane” and their Russian-language equivalents for 2000–2024. Of the 412 studies retrieved, 87 containing quantitative flux estimates and a description of the methodology were selected after screening of abstracts and full texts.
body.v1n1-04-peatland-carbon.methods.1: For each study, the peatland type, its condition (undisturbed, drained, under restoration), the measurement method, the duration of observations and the balance components accounted for were recorded. Estimates of net ecosystem exchange were converted to units of g C/m² per year.
body.v1n1-04-peatland-carbon.results.0: The distribution of studies by method is uneven (Fig. 1): almost half of the studies are based on the chamber method, and about a third on the eddy covariance method. Remote sensing approaches are used mainly for upscaling rather than as a stand-alone source of estimates.
body.v1n1-04-peatland-carbon.results.1: Comparative characteristics of the methods are given in Table 1. The chamber method makes it possible to partition fluxes by microlandscape but describes temporal variability poorly; the eddy covariance method yields continuous time series but requires a homogeneous site and expensive equipment.
body.v1n1-04-peatland-carbon.figure.capt: Fig. 1. Distribution of the reviewed studies by primary assessment method (n = 87)
body.v1n1-04-peatland-carbon.table.capti: Table 1. Comparison of methods for assessing the carbon balance of peatlands
The substantial discrepancies between methods are explained not so much by measurement errors as by differences in the balance components accounted for. Studies that do not account for the export of dissolved organic carbon with peatland waters systematically overestimate the carbon sink by 10–25%.

Peatlands under restoration remain the least studied: in the first years after rewetting, methane emissions may temporarily increase, which must be taken into account when assessing the climatic effect of restoration projects.
None of the methods provides a complete assessment of the carbon balance of peatlands. The optimal solution appears to be a network of reference sites with long-term eddy covariance observations, supplemented by chamber measurements and remote sensing upscaling.
The business press is one of the main channels for the dissemination of economic terminology: new concepts appear there earlier than in dictionaries and textbooks. In 2015–2024, the digitalisation of trade, finance and labour was accompanied by a particularly intensive expansion of the vocabulary.
The aim of this communication is to describe the composition and dynamics of digital economy neologisms in the business media and to characterise the main ways in which they are formed.

The corpus was compiled from openly accessible publications of six business outlets (designated P1–P6) and morphologically annotated. Neologism candidates were selected as lemmas that were absent from the 2010–2014 subcorpus and occurred at least 20 times in 2015–2024. Two experts then independently verified whether the units belonged to the subject area of the digital economy; inter-expert agreement (Cohen’s κ) was 0.82.

The final list comprises 214 units. The distribution by year of first attestation is shown in Fig. 1: the peak falls in 2018–2020, which coincides with the period of active growth of online retail and platform employment. The distribution by method of formation is given in Table 1.
Fig. 1. Number of new units by year of first attestation in the corpus
Table 1. Neologisms by method of formation
цифровой след ‘digital footprint’, умный контракт ‘smart contract’

The predominance of direct borrowings is to be expected in a rapidly developing subject area. At the same time, the high share of hybrid formations shows that borrowed stems are quickly integrated into the Russian word-formation system. The displacement of Latin-script spellings by Cyrillic ones (for example, for the word стартап ‘startup’ the share of Latin-script spellings fell from 34% in 2015 to 3% in 2024) serves as an indicator of assimilation.

The corpus-based approach makes it possible to date the emergence and assimilation of new economic vocabulary objectively. The resulting list of neologisms may serve as the basis for a specialised dictionary.
Over the past fifteen years, the power conversion efficiency of perovskite solar cells has risen from a few per cent to values comparable with those of silicon cells. The main obstacle to commercialisation remains stability: under the action of moisture, light and temperature, the perovskite crystal lattice decomposes with the formation of lead iodide.

Thermal cycling — repeated temperature changes — is one of the most severe tests, since the mismatch between the thermal expansion coefficients of the film and the substrate leads to the accumulation of mechanical stress. The aim of the study is to compare the effectiveness of three organic additives of different nature in improving the resistance of films to thermal cycling.
body.v1n2-01-perovskite-stability.method: Films of a mixed-cation perovskite based on caesium, formamidinium and methylammonium (CsFAMA) with partial substitution of iodine by bromine (15%) were deposited on glass substrates with a conductive coating by spin coating with dropwise addition of an antisolvent and annealed at 100 °C. The additives were introduced into the precursor solution: phenethylammonium iodide (PEA, 1.5 mol%), thiourea (TU, 3 mol%) and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP, 0.5 wt%).

Thermal cycling was carried out in a climatic chamber under an inert atmosphere: one cycle comprised a 15-min dwell at −20 °C and a 15-min dwell at +85 °C with a temperature ramp rate of 5 °C/min. After 0, 50, 100 and 200 cycles, the samples were examined by X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy and steady-state photoluminescence.
body.v1n2-01-perovskite-stability.result: The change in integrated photoluminescence intensity as a function of the number of cycles is shown in Fig. 1. In the control samples, the intensity decreases to 54% of the initial value after 100 cycles and to 31% after 200 cycles; at the same time, a lead iodide reflection at 2θ = 12.7° appears in the diffraction patterns.

The highest stability was demonstrated by the PEA films, in which no secondary phases were detected even after 200 cycles. The addition of PVP almost completely suppresses the formation of microcracks but does not prevent a gradual decrease in photoluminescence intensity. Summary characteristics are given in Table 1.
body.v1n2-01-perovskite-stability.figure: Fig. 1. Relative photoluminescence intensity of the films as a function of the number of thermal cycles, %
Table 1. Characteristics of the films before and after 200 cycles
body.v1n2-01-perovskite-stability.discus: The stabilising effect of PEA can be explained by the formation of a thin layer of two-dimensional perovskite on the grain surfaces, which passivates defects and hinders the migration of halide ions. PVP apparently acts differently: polymer chains localised at the grain boundaries partially relax mechanical stresses and prevent cracking.

The difference in mechanisms opens up the possibility of using the additives in combination. Preliminary experiments with the simultaneous introduction of PEA and PVP show retention of 91% of the photoluminescence intensity after 200 cycles, which requires further verification in complete solar cells.
body.v1n2-01-perovskite-stability.conclu: Phenethylammonium is the most effective of the additives studied for improving the resistance of perovskite films to thermal cycling, while polyvinylpyrrolidone effectively suppresses cracking. Combining additives with different mechanisms of action appears to be a promising strategy.
body.v1n2-02-adaptive-courses.intro.0: The transition from school to university is accompanied by a sharp change in the demands placed on students’ independence. According to data from many universities, the largest share of students drop out in the first year, and mathematical subjects become the main “filter”. The reason lies largely in the heterogeneity of school preparation, which is difficult to compensate for within whole-class instruction.
body.v1n2-02-adaptive-courses.intro.1: Adaptive learning systems, which select tasks according to a student’s individual level, are regarded as a way of approaching the effect of one-to-one tutoring. However, rigorous evaluations of their effectiveness in Russian universities are scarce. The present study estimates the effect of an adaptive calculus course on the performance of first-year students.
body.v1n2-02-adaptive-courses.methods.0: The adaptive course comprised 14 thematic modules and a bank of 1,860 tasks annotated with typical errors. After each task, the system updated its estimate of skill mastery using a Bayesian knowledge tracing model and offered the next task or explanatory material. The course was used as a compulsory part of independent study.
body.v1n2-02-adaptive-courses.methods.1: The experimental group consisted of 214 students admitted in 2023, and the control group of 198 students admitted in 2022 who were taught by the same instructors under the same curriculum with traditional homework assignments. Matching was based on a propensity score estimated by logistic regression on total entrance scores, sex and school type; after matching, 181 pairs were included in the analysis.
body.v1n2-02-adaptive-courses.results.0: After matching, the mean final examination score was 68.9 in the experimental group and 61.5 in the control group (a difference of 7.4 points; 95% CI: 4.1–10.7). The distribution of the effect across quartiles of entrance scores is shown in Fig. 1: the largest gain is observed in the lowest quartile.
body.v1n2-02-adaptive-courses.results.1: Analysis of the system logs showed that the number of weeks of active work is more strongly associated with the final score (r = 0.52) than the total time spent (r = 0.29). The main results are given in Table 1.
body.v1n2-02-adaptive-courses.figure.cap: Fig. 1. Mean examination score by quartile of entrance scores

body.v1n2-02-adaptive-courses.discussion: The effect obtained is comparable with the results of international meta-analyses of adaptive practice in higher education. Its concentration in the group of students with weak preparation indicates that adaptive courses are capable of partially compensating for differences in starting conditions.

The quasi-experimental design does not make it possible to rule out entirely the influence of differences between the intake cohorts of different years that were not accounted for in matching. Nevertheless, the fact that the instructors, curriculum and examination format were the same reduces the risk of bias. The finding on the importance of regular work has a direct practical implication: weekly checkpoints may strengthen the effect.
body.v1n2-02-adaptive-courses.conclusion: The adaptive online calculus course improved the academic performance of first-year students and reduced the share of unsatisfactory results, especially among students with low entrance scores. It is recommended that adaptive courses be combined with mechanisms that support regular work.
body.v1n2-04-computing-centres-history.i: The advent of electronic computers in the late 1940s and 1950s required the creation of special institutions: the machines were expensive, occupied entire halls and required round-the-clock maintenance. Computing centres became places where engineers, mathematicians and scientific users met, and where new professions — the programmer and the operator — gradually took shape.

The historiography of computing centres developed together with the history of computing itself as a discipline. The aim of this review is to systematise approaches to the study of these institutions, identify understudied topics and discuss the state of the source base.
body.v1n2-04-computing-centres-history.m: The review corpus was compiled from the bibliographies of key works and the subject indexes of specialist journals on the history of science and technology. Studies were included in which a computing centre (rather than an individual machine or person) is the subject of analysis in at least one chapter or section. The final corpus comprised 64 works published between 1975 and 2024.

Each work was classified by its leading approach, the type of sources used and the geography of the institutions studied. The classification was performed by the author and re-checked a year later to assess its consistency.
body.v1n2-04-computing-centres-history.r: The distribution of works by decade and approach is shown in Fig. 1. Until the 1990s, the technical-biographical approach dominated, represented mainly by participants’ memoirs and anniversary publications. Institutional studies became prominent in the 1990s–2000s, and studies of practices after 2010.

Table 1 shows which sources are used within the different approaches. Notably, machine-time logs and surviving program texts are drawn upon in only a small proportion of works, even though they make it possible to reconstruct the actual workload of the machines and the range of problems solved.
body.v1n2-04-computing-centres-history.f: Fig. 1. Number of works by decade of publication and leading approach
body.v1n2-04-computing-centres-history.t: Table 1. Types of sources by historiographical approach (share of works, %)
body.v1n2-04-computing-centres-history.d: The shift in approaches reflects the general evolution of the history of science from a history of discoveries and inventors towards a social history of knowledge and a history of practices. At the same time, technical-biographical works retain their value as a source of factual information, especially when they are based on documents inaccessible to researchers.

The main gaps concern the “invisible” participants in computing work — operators, keypunch operators and programmers, many of whom were women — and regional centres. The time available for recording interviews with participants in these events is limited, which makes oral history projects particularly pressing.
body.v1n2-04-computing-centres-history.c: The historiography of computing centres has moved from a history of machines to a history of practices. Further progress requires broadening the source base — a systematic search for machine-time logs and programs — and combining archival work with oral history.
body.v1n2-05-greywater-reuse.intro.0: About a third of the drinking water consumed in residential buildings is used for toilet flushing and irrigation — purposes for which drinking-water quality is not required. Greywater from showers and washbasins accounts for up to 60% of household wastewater and is relatively lightly polluted, which makes it an attractive source for non-potable water supply.
body.v1n2-05-greywater-reuse.intro.1: The aim of this communication is to present the results of one year of pilot operation of a greywater reuse system in a multi-apartment residential block and to assess its effectiveness, cost-efficiency and perception by residents.
body.v1n2-05-greywater-reuse.methods.0: The pilot block comprises three ten-storey buildings with separate internal sewerage for greywater and blackwater. A treatment unit with a capacity of 25 m³/day is located in the basement. The volumes of incoming greywater, treated water and make-up water from the municipal network were recorded by automatic flow meters; the quality of treated water was monitored weekly by an accredited laboratory. At the end of the period, a questionnaire survey of residents was conducted (n = 163).
body.v1n2-05-greywater-reuse.results.0: The mean daily volume of reused water was 14.6 m³. The monthly share of drinking water substitution is shown in Fig. 1: the lowest values were recorded in winter (22–24%) and the highest in July and August (33–34%). Treated water quality indicators are given in Table 1.
body.v1n2-05-greywater-reuse.figure.capt: Fig. 1. Share of drinking water substituted by treated greywater by month, %
body.v1n2-05-greywater-reuse.table.capti: Table 1. Treated water quality (mean over 52 weeks)
The substitution share obtained is close to the theoretical potential for this type of housing. Cost-efficiency depends strongly on water tariffs: as they rise, the payback period shortens to 6–7 years. Importantly, residents perceive the technology positively; however, any deviation in the organoleptic properties of the water quickly undermines trust, so reliable disinfection and monitoring are critical.
The greywater reuse system made it possible to reduce drinking water consumption by a quarter, with the treated water consistently meeting the standards. The technology can be recommended for new multi-apartment residential developments.
